lead.hed: Nimitz certified its landing system on the first underway since the move to Norfolk
lead.insight: DVIDS reported that USS Nimitz conducted Precision Approach Landing Systems certification from Oct. 5 through Oct. 8, its first underway since the homeport shift to Norfolk in July. The release says the system, run by the combat systems department and the carrier air traffic control center, guides pilots to a starting position for night and bad-weather landings, and that a ship needs it before flight operations. Sailors also drilled aircraft recovery, damage control, and propulsion. The release says the certification prepares the ship for east-coast carrier qualifications, the first time student naval aviators land on an operational flight deck, and that several of those periods are scheduled for Commander, Naval Air Force Atlantic. Nimitz is homeported at Naval Station Norfolk in Carrier Strike Group 8. The still shows the aviation refueling team preparing a line on the flight deck in the Atlantic on Oct. 6.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist 3rd Class Matthew C. Wolf · DVIDS 9998635 · Public domain · Aviation refueling team Sailors prepare a line on the flight deck of USS Nimitz in the Atlantic Ocean. Photo taken Oct. 6, 2026.

political.hed: Heritage says states still have to do the work of securing elections
political.insight: Friday's commentary says Americans cannot treat election security as settled. The writer argues the right to vote is not self-executing, and that laws have to administer it and defend it against error, fraud, and foreign interference. It is a call for state administration, not a new federal statute posted with the piece.

political.hed: Law & Liberty says a Washington statue in Budapest shows what assimilation once looked like
political.insight: Friday's essay says the George Washington statue beside a lake in Budapest's City Park was paid for by Hungarian immigrants in the United States, not by a government exchange. The writer contrasts it with the diplomatic monuments in Paris and London, and treats the gift as a case of people who left a country and still honored the one they joined. It is an argument about immigration and gratitude, not a bill.

tech.hed: The Army activated a new Indo-Pacific fires task force at Fort Carson
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that the 4th Multi-Domain Task Force activated Thursday at Founder's Field on Fort Carson. The Army said the unit will synchronize long-range precision fires in the Indo-Pacific to deny, disrupt, and disaggregate adversary capabilities. It has four battalions and is planned to grow to 2,100 soldiers. Col. Hugh W.A. Jones took command. The task force reports to the 7th Infantry Division at Joint Base Lewis-McChord. The ceremony is an activation, not a deployment order.

tech.hed: The Army awarded Kaizen a contract for software above its systems of record
tech.insight: Defense News reported Saturday that the Army awarded Kaizen Laboratories $43 million to build application software for highly sensitive military material. A company release calls the vehicle a $49 million five-year enterprise agreement, covering mission applications, staff workflows, records, and reporting that sit above the Army's systems of record. Chief executive Nikhil Reddy said the remaining $6 million could fund readiness, personnel, installations, logistics, or operations software if demand rises. In August the same company built the Pentagon's counter-drone marketplace with the joint counter-drone task force. This is a framework the Army can order against, not a fielded system.

culture.hed: WORLD reviews Sorkin's Facebook film as a journalism thriller with a paywall of its own
culture.insight: Thursday's review covers Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning, a follow-on to The Social Network, set around the 2021 Facebook Files. The readable opening quotes a Wall Street Journal reporter telling a Facebook employee that a story is not facts. WORLD rates the film R and in theaters. The rest of the review sits behind the magazine's subscription wall, so this item stops at what the public page actually shows.

culture.hed: American Reformer says Cornell promotes sexual liberation and then acts shocked
culture.insight: Thursday's essay argues the national story out of Cornell is moral hysteria, and that the public record so far, including a signed statement, describes consensual sex rather than rape. The writer says universities publish sexual-liberation guidance and then punish the conduct that guidance invites. It is an argument about campus rules, not a court judgment.

watch.hed: Raytheon has a $6.3 billion deal to replenish SM-3 Block IB interceptors
watch.note: Defense News, Friday, citing Raytheon's Thursday announcement. Five-year contract, two option years, production mainly in Tucson and Huntsville. No official still staged as the lead.

watch.hed: Ships in the Strait of Hormuz have been hit nearly every day this month
